subject: general
question:
Read the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) carefully and choose the correct option:

Assertion (A) The New Economic Policy of 1991 led to more efficient and competitive markets in India.

Reason (R): Privatization reduced government control and improved productivity in public enterprises.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false​A
A is false, but R is true​

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A):** The **New Economic Policy of 1991** led to more efficient and competitive markets in India. This is **correct**. The 1991 reforms introduced measures such as **liberalization, privatization, and globalization**, which reduced trade barriers and restrictions, opening up the economy to competition and efficiency.
 
• **Reason (R):** Privatization reduced government control and improved productivity in public enterprises. This is also **correct**. Privatization allowed private sectors to take over previously government-controlled businesses, leading to better management practices, increased productivity, and higher efficiency.
 
• The **Reason (R)** explains the **Assertion (A)** accurately. Privatization was a significant part of the 1991 reforms that contributed to the creation of competitive markets and improved the overall economic structure. *Hence, Option 1 is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **New Economic Policy of 1991:**

 
 
• Introduced by the **Government of India** under **Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao** and **Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh**.
 
• Focused on three pillars: **liberalization** (removal of restrictions and licensing), **privatization** (transfer of ownership from public to private), and **globalization** (integration with the global economy).
 
• Aimed to address the **balance of payments crisis** and economic stagnation, and to improve market efficiency.
 
• Key reforms included the abolition of the **License Raj**, reduction of tariffs, removal of trade barriers, and encouragement of foreign investments.
 
 
 
• **Privatization:**
 
 
• Involved transferring ownership of public sector enterprises to private entities to enhance efficiency and productivity.
 
• Led to better management practices and reduced bureaucratic inefficiencies.
 
• Examples: Disinvestment of companies like **Air India**, **VSNL**, and **Maruti Suzuki**.
 
 
 
• **Impact of New Economic Policy:**
 
 
• **Economic growth:** India's GDP grew significantly after the reforms.
 
• **Foreign investment:** Increased Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) inflows.
 
• **Competitive markets:** Removal of monopolies led to a more competitive environment.
 
• **Global integration:** India became a significant player in the global market.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key features of 1991 reforms:**

 
 
• **Liberalization:** Removed licensing and regulatory hurdles for businesses.
 
• **Privatization:** Focused on disinvesting public enterprises to improve efficiency.
 
• **Globalization:** Opened up the economy to foreign investment and trade.
 
 
 
• **Challenges and criticisms:**
 
 
• **Income inequality:** Critics argue that the reforms widened the gap between rich and poor.
 
• **Dependency on foreign investment:** Concerns over excessive reliance on foreign capital.
 
• **Environmental impact:** Increased industrialization led to ecological concerns.
